alt.en: One line of printed music in 3/4 with one flat, headed "(4.)" at the left and signed "Schulz." at the right, with two small entry marks above the staff and, under it, the German words in black-letter type: "O wie wohl ist mir am Abend, wenn zur Ruh die Glocken läuten: bum, bum, bum, bum."
alt.es: Una línea de música impresa en 3/4 con un bemol en la clave, encabezada "(4.)" a la izquierda y firmada "Schulz." a la derecha, con dos pequeñas marcas de entrada sobre el pentagrama y, debajo, la letra alemana en letra gótica: "O wie wohl ist mir am Abend, wenn zur Ruh die Glocken läuten: bum, bum, bum, bum."

caption.en: The fourth of the "Vier Canons", four canons, on page 193 of Liederlust und Psalter, a German-language songbook printed in Cincinnati in 1882: the earliest printing we read that names a Schulz for the round, signed simply "Schulz."
caption.es: El cuarto de los "Vier Canons", cuatro cánones, en la página 193 de Liederlust und Psalter, un cancionero en alemán impreso en Cincinnati en 1882: la impresión más antigua que leímos que nombra a un Schulz para el canon, firmado simplemente "Schulz."

source: H. Liebhart, Liederlust und Psalter (Cincinnati: Cranston und Stowe, 1882), p. 193, No. 186, "Vier Canons", No. 4 (cropped to that canon)
library: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive liederlustundpsa00lieb_0; UNC record b76013108
licenceEvidence: Printed Cincinnati 1882; editor Henry Liebhart 1832-1895; the canon signed "Schulz" (Karl Friedrich Schulz died 1850). Faithful scan of a flat page, cropped (see rights.md).
credit: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: Part of a printed music page headed "OH, HOW LOVELY! (ROUND FOR THREE VOICES.)", three staves in 6/8 with one sharp, numbered 2, 3, 1 at the right (the 1, 2, 3 at the left are cut by the edge of the scan), with the words "Oh how love-ly is the eve-ning, is the eve-ning,", "When to rest the bells are ring-ing, bells are ring-ing!" and "Bome! bome! bome! bome! bome! bome", and the page number 41.
alt.es: Parte de una página de música impresa con el título "OH, HOW LOVELY! (ROUND FOR THREE VOICES.)", tres pentagramas en 6/8 con un sostenido en la clave, numerados 2, 3, 1 a la derecha (el 1, 2, 3 de la izquierda queda cortado por el borde del escaneo), con la letra "Oh how love-ly is the eve-ning, is the eve-ning,", "When to rest the bells are ring-ing, bells are ring-ing!" y "Bome! bome! bome! bome! bome! bome", y el número de página 41.

caption.en: Page 41 of Henry Francis Sefton's Three-Part Songs for the public schools of Canada (Toronto, 1869): the earliest English version we found, a round for three voices whose third line rings "Bome!" six times on one note.
caption.es: La página 41 de Three-Part Songs, de Henry Francis Sefton, para las escuelas públicas de Canadá (Toronto, 1869): la versión inglesa más antigua que encontramos, un canon a tres voces cuyo tercer verso repica "Bome!" seis veces en una misma nota.

source: Henry Francis Sefton, Three-Part Songs for the Use of the Pupils of the Public Schools of Canada (Toronto: James Campbell and Son, 1869), p. 41, "Oh, How Lovely! (Round for Three Voices.)" (cropped to the round)
library: The University of Western Ontario, Western Archives (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed Toronto 1869; Henry Francis Sefton died 1892; the round's English words anonymous. Faithful scan of a flat page, cropped (see rights.md).
credit: The University of Western Ontario, Western Archives, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a large empty hall: rows of curved wooden seats, slender dark iron columns with a Greek-key band at the top, broad stone-coloured arches and vaults overhead with hanging lamps, and a low platform with folding chairs at the left.
alt.es: Una fotografía en blanco y negro de una gran sala vacía: filas de asientos curvos de madera, delgadas columnas oscuras de hierro con una greca en lo alto, anchos arcos y bóvedas de color piedra con lámparas colgantes y, a la izquierda, una tarima baja con sillas plegables.

caption.en: The Great Hall of Cooper Union in New York, photographed for the Historic American Engineering Record in about 1971: at Cooper Union in October 1892, 2,500 came to Frank Damrosch's first People's Singing Class, sang, Harper's Weekly wrote, "till the vaulted arches rang", and learned this round.
caption.es: El Great Hall (gran salón) de la Cooper Union de Nueva York, fotografiado para el Historic American Engineering Record hacia 1971: en la Cooper Union, en octubre de 1892, 2500 personas acudieron a la primera People's Singing Class (clase de canto para el pueblo) de Frank Damrosch, cantaron, según Harper's Weekly, "hasta que resonaron los arcos abovedados" y aprendieron este canon.

source: Historic American Engineering Record, Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art, Third and Fourth Avenues, Astor Place, Seventh Street, New York County, NY (survey HAER NY-20), photograph 10, Jack E. Boucher, photographer (cropped: the right-hand wall, with its framed pictures, is left out)

alt.en: Printed music headed "ROUND.": three staves in 3/4 with one flat, marked I, II and III, with the words "O how love-ly is the even-ing, is the even-ing,", "When the bells are sweet-ly ring-ing, sweet-ly ring-ing:" and "Ding, dong, ding, dong, ding, dong!", the third line six long notes on one pitch.
alt.es: Música impresa con el título "ROUND.": tres pentagramas en 3/4 con un bemol en la clave, marcados I, II y III, con la letra "O how love-ly is the even-ing, is the even-ing,", "When the bells are sweet-ly ring-ing, sweet-ly ring-ing:" y "Ding, dong, ding, dong, ding, dong!", el tercer verso con seis notas largas en una misma altura.

caption.en: Page 22 of The Educational Music Course, First Reader (Boston, copyright 1896): the round in three lines marked I, II and III, in F and in 3/4, the page our arrangement is read from, a whole tone lower.
caption.es: La página 22 de The Educational Music Course, First Reader (Boston, copyright de 1896): el canon en tres versos marcados I, II y III, en Fa y en 3/4, la página de la que está tomado nuestro arreglo, un tono más abajo.

source: Luther Whiting Mason, James M. McLaughlin, George A. Veazie, W. W. Gilchrist and Nathan Haskell Dole, The Educational Music Course: First Reader (Boston and London: Ginn & Company, copyright 1896), p. 22, "Round." (cropped to the round)
library: Harvard University (digitized by Google; Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Copyright 1896, US (title page dated 1898); editors died 1896 to 1935 (Dole the last, 1935); the round's words anonymous. Faithful scan of a flat page, cropped (see rights.md).
